title: LPU BAGS THIRD POSITION IN TECHNO QUIZ BY AIMLTA (4/22/2011)
body: Students of Paramedical Sciences, LPU (Lovely Professional University, Phagwara) attended conference of All India Medical Laboratory Technologists Association (AIMLTA) at Govt Medical College & Hospital, Sec-32, Chandigarh on 15th April 2011 to celebrate World Biomedical Laboratory Science Day. Scientific seminars on various issues of current concern like use of untested, unsafe & unnecessary vaccines, mobile phones as a risk to human, diagnosis of deadly TB, quality control of coagulation testing, preanalytical phase quality collection were held. Delegates from all over north India attended this conference. A Techno Quiz was organized where Jasmine Shrivastav, Rahul Raina & Surbhi students of M Sc Clinical Microbiology, LPU won the third prize whereas First & second positions bagged by PGIMER, Chandigarh. Fourteen teams from twelve different Institutes located in Uttranchal, Chandigarh, & Punjab participated. Quiz had three rounds comprising technical questions, visual display, and rapid fire. This was the great achievement for the students of department of Paramedical Sciences, LSPPS, LPU. They have been ranked the best among all other Paramedical colleges of North India. Attachment: TECHNO QUIZ BY AIMLTA.jpg The students of LPU were honoured by Mr. AP Chauhan (Dept. Haematology PGIMER Chd.) Authorized By: Office of HOD Deptt: Paramedical Sciences

For any further clarification, contact Division of Examination Block No.32, Room No.101, Ph.01824-506652. title: RESULTS OF ARMAGEDDON-the rock show: OFFICIAL VIDEO MUSIC ALBUM (4/11/2011)
body: Armageddon-the rock show was held on 9th April 2011 in front of Campus Café with an objective of selecting the most suitable band for recording a track for the upcoming first official video music album. The beauty of event was that the most experienced rock band of LPU shared the same stage as a band that performed on stage for the first time (RHYTHMIC BOYS). There were six bands in competition with two others as guest performers. “PROVISK” won the competition and hence shall be recording a track for the album. Congratulations to “PROVISK”. But the show and the heart of the judges was stolen by “AGRAATH” by three back to back performances on original compositions. The judges urged the project head to approach “SA-RE-GA-MA-PA” who are presently looking for young desi rock bands like “AGRAATH”. The group leader of “AGRAATH”, Mr. Sankalp Singha, having been the best in “MUSIC MANIA COMPETITION” is presently working on the music compositions for the album. We congratulate AGRAATH for the fabulous performance. The judges also commented that the young Indian bands should promote Indian languages even though adopting the western rock style. Congratulations to all participating team for making the event a success. Deepak Sameer Jha Project Head Official Video Music Album 9464108712 Authorized By: Asst. Director Department of Cultural Affairs

title: KPMG Six Sigma (Green Belt) Program Registration Re - Opens (4/1/2011)
body: Registration for KPMG Six Sigma Green Belt Program has been re opened. Previous fee for KPMG Six Sigma Program Rs 3850 was subject to minimum 150 Registrations. As students did not turn up for the registration, and the required number of registrations 150 was not achieved, fee has gone up with minimum registration of 60 to start the program. For your reference profile of the trainers have been attached herewith. --------------------------------------------------------------------------- Six Sigma is a management methodology meant for driving process improvements in the delivery of goods and services. It provides businesses with the tools to improve the capability of their business processes. The increase in performance and decrease in process variation leads to defect reduction and vast improvement in profits, employee morale and quality of product. KPMG is world top consultancy firm. KPMG in India is one of the leading providers of risk, financial and business advisory, internal audit, corporate governance, and tax and regulatory services. With a global approach to service delivery, KPMG responds to clients complex business challenges with a broad range of services across industry sectors and national boundaries. KPMG in India has developed a balanced program, specific to the needs of students, that allows your transformation into an effective change agent, who can, using the Six Sigma framework bring about significant improvements in the organizations performance. LPU and KPMG have come together to provide SIX Sigma Green Belt program that will provide up skilling to all the graduates irrespective of their stream. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- Eligibility: All Engineering/Management/Applied Medical Sciences/CAP Graduates Certification Involved: Yes (By KPMG) Registration Fee: Rs 500 Total fee (includes reg. fee): Rs 6000 + Taxes (Includes certification by KPMG and Course Content, and all taxes, registration fee involved) Timings: Seats: Minimum 60 to start the course How to register: 1 Register by filling the form attached herewith and pay registration fee (Rs 500) at Accounts Office. Copy of the fee receipt need to be deposited along with the form at DSCS, 304/32, by 16th April, 2011. 2 Last date to pay remaining fee to confirm your seat is 30th April, 2011. 3 Fee can be deposited in cash only Important Dates to Remember: Course Commencement Date: 20th and 21st August, 2011 Last date to register online: 27th and 28th August, 2011 Last date to Register: 16th April, 2011 Last date to pay remaining fee at Accounts Office and submit a copy of fee receipt at DSCS: 30th April, 2011 For any further information/clarity, contact Mr Anil Kumar, 09780005949, anil.kumar@lpu.co.in Attachments: 1.Ajay Chugh _April 1.pdf 2.Literature_Notice Board_April 1.doc 3.Nitesh Jain_KPMG_Short_April 1.pdf 4.Registration form for KPMG_April 1.doc Authorized By: Office of the HOD Department of Placements Division of Student Career services

title: WEARING OF MOBILE EAR PLUGS BY STUDENTS (3/31/2011)
body: 1. It has come to the notice of the University Authorities that certain students of University are in the habit of wearing mobile ear plugs and listening to music while walking around in the Campus and also on NH-1 (GT Road) while entering and exiting the University. Wearing of mobile ear plugs and listening to music create an illusionary sensing thereby the concerned person is not aware of the other factors around him such as movement of cars, bikes etc. which may cause serious injuries. 2. In view of this, all students are hereby advised that henceforth, within the University and outside University Main Entrance Gates and at other public places, students should not wear mobile ear plugs, this can lead to any kind of mishappening or accident. Authorized By: Brig. (Retd.) G.S. Dhillon Chief Security Officer Deptt: Security & Discipline

title: Notice for Scrutiny of MTE March 2011 (For Back Log courses) (3/22/2011)
body: All students are hereby informed to note that the Scrutiny of Answer Sheets of MTE March 2011 for Back Log courses is scheduled to be held from 24.3.2011 (Thursday) to 26.3.2011 (Saturday). The Scrutiny will be conducted daily from 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. in Room No. 32-508, 32-510 & 32-512. Only those students who were unable to see their answer sheets for MTE March 2011 of Back Log courses may visit the above mentioned for Scrutiny. The students must follow the following instructions properly: - 1. Students will be given the Evaluated Answer Scripts for at the most five minutes. 2. Student can go through his/her Evaluated Answer Script and write request / remark on the space provided on the Front Page of the Answer Sheet with Pencil only. 3. Discussion with other students or exchanging the answer sheets with other students is not allowed and might call for UMC. 4. Except writing the remarks / requests, no other change in the answer scripts is to be done by the student. 5. Student is allowed to write only three type of remarks as mentioned below: (a) Any question or part thereof not graded. (b) Marks awarded for a question in the Answer Sheet does not match with the marks written on the front page. (c) Any type of totaling or clerical mistake 6. Re-grading / Rectification of error (Sr. No. 5a) will be done by the concerned evaluator who has originally graded the particular question and a comment shall be made on the answer sheet under the signature of the evaluator 7. The scope for re-grading will be restricted strictly to the comments of the students on the cover of the answer-book during the process of showing answer sheets to the students. 8. Writing with a pen or writing anywhere other than at specified place or not returning the Answer Sheets or any other disobedience will result in UMC case. 9. If any student does not abide by the clauses mentioned above, UMC may be filed against him. Examination Division Authorized By: Office of Deputy Dean Deptt: Examination Division

title: PROJECTVILLA (3/22/2011)
body: PROJECTVILLA will be conducting workshops for all interested students on various topics as: Digital Image Processing, Android App. Development, Mobile Robotics, and CV based Autonomous Robots Development in LPU from 25th March,2011 to 17th April,2011. Content: Above mentioned technical workshops are paid and prerequisite for them is that the student should have the basic knowledge of any programming language. First of all student should register on the following link: http://www.projectvilla.com/regis.php , Register themselves , take print out of registration slip and take that registration slip to accounts and then they have to deposit the fees by cash in Accounts Department, LPU as fee mentioned in table below. Last date of registration and fee submission is 25th March, 2011. After registration students should have to submit registration slip to Accounts Department along with the fees as mentioned in below table. Original fee receipts should be submitted to Mr. Anurag Verma, AP-ECE, LHST-LPU latest by 26-03-2011 in block 26-205. Any student, no matter what year or branch, can participate in the workshop if he/she has basic knowledge of any programming language. The workshops will be done in two sessions. Session 1 will be held on Saturday from 4pm to 6pm. Session 2 will be held on Sunday from 10am to 4pm. All participants are expected to carry a laptop along with Dev C++ installed on it. Students interested in Android Application Development Workshop are expected to have Java JDK, Eclipse and Android SDK Plug-in installed on their systems. Students interested in Digital Image processing Workshop are expected to install any Car racing game, whether demo version or full, preferably Need for Speed. Charges for workshops are as follows: TOPICS DURATION(HOURS) CHARGES PER PARTICIPATION(RUPEES) DATES Digital Image Processing 8 hrs 800 26th and 27th March 2011 Android App development 8 Hrs 800 9th and 10th April 2011 Mobile robotics 8-10 Hrs 1000 9th and 10th April 2011 CV Based Autonomous robots 8-10 Hrs 1000 16th and 17th April 2011 Industry Interface Group-LFTS, LPU, will co-ordinate the workshops with PROJECTVILLA. For any query please contact Mr. Anurag Verma, Mob: 09815475530. He will also be available in 26-205 from 3pm to 5pm on 19-03-2011. Authorized By: Office of HOD Deptt: ECE LHST

body: Thyrocare has openings in the Administration, HRD, IT, Laboratory in their Mumbai Office and in Marketing, Sales and Business Development pan India. They are looking to hire from the follwing streams: 1. M.Sc- Biotechnology / M.Sc- Microbiology 2. B.Sc- Biotechnology / B.Sc- Microbiology 3. B.Tech-Biotech 4. M.Tech- Biotech 5. M.Sc-Biochemistry 6. B.Sc- MLT 7. title: PROJECTVILLA will be conducting workshops for all interested students. (3/19/2011)
body: PROJECTVILLA will be conducting workshops for all interested students on various topics as: Digital Image Processing, Android App. Development, Mobile Robotics, and CV based Autonomous Robots Development in LPU from 25th March,2011 to 17th April,2011. Above mentioned technical workshops are paid and prerequisite for them is that the student should have the basic knowledge of any programming language. First of all student should register on the following link: http://www.projectvilla.com/regis.php , Register themselves , take print out of registration slip and take that registration slip to accounts and then they have to deposit the fees by cash in Accounts Department, LPU as fee mentioned in table below. Last date of registration and fee submission is 25th March, 2011. After registration students should have to submit registration slip to Accounts Department along with the fees as mentioned in below table. Original fee receipts should be submitted to Mr. Anurag Verma, AP-ECE, LHST-LPU latest by 26-03-2011 in block 26-205. Any student, no matter what year or branch, can participate in the workshop if he/she has basic knowledge of any programming language. The workshops will be done in two sessions. Session 1 will be held on Saturday from 4pm to 6pm. Session 2 will be held on Sunday from 10am to 4pm. All participants are expected to carry a laptop along with Dev C++ installed on it. Students interested in Android Application Development Workshop are expected to have Java JDK, Eclipse and Android SDK Plug-in installed on their systems. Students interested in Digital Image processing Workshop are expected to install any Car racing game, whether demo version or full, preferably Need for Speed. Charges for workshops are as follows: TOPICS DURATION(HOURS) CHARGES PER PARTICIPATION(RUPEES) DATES Digital Image Processing 8 hrs 800 26th and 27th March 2011 Android App development 8 Hrs 800 9th and 10th April 2011 Mobile robotics 8-10 Hrs 1000 9th and 10th April 2011 CV Based Autonomous robots 8-10 Hrs 1000 16th and 17th April 2011 Industry Interface Group-LFTS, LPU, will co-ordinate the workshops with PROJECTVILLA. For any query please contact Mr. Anurag Verma, Mob: 09815475530. He will also be available in 26-205 from 3pm to 5pm on 19-03-2011. Authorized By: Office of HOD Deptt: ECE LHST

title: INVICTUS 11…… Renaissance of the Technical Geeks (3/16/2011)
body: "Genius is the ability to put into effect what is in your mind." This April, fear will fall and courage will rise in a series of fierce battles, covering all the fields from advanced coding to simple logic, from algorithm design to computer fundamentals. Lectures, project displays & events that are mind freaking & breath taking will also be witnessed. All you need is the creativity, enthusiasm and the courage to be pitted against the best, and you could be one of the warriors here. The stage is set and if you think you have it in you, then adorn your armour, sharpen your minds, unleash your ideas and get ready for INVICTUS 11 - A TechFest brought to you by the Department of Computer Applications on 15th & 16th April 2011. Events of the TechFest are:- • Coding Maestros - Join the battle of codes • Reign of Errors – Smash the bug • Project-o-Holic - Talk of technology and what a better place to witness it • Guest Lectures - Exotic topics and informative insights • Query Fury – Can you generate a mind-boggling query? • Mind Vision - Draw what you like • Tech Adventure - A treasure hunt... but with a difference! • Fanatic Brains - Animate the world around you • AlgoRhythm Tailor – Do you find it a challenge to build algorithms? • Game-O-Sphere – Everything from Formula-1 cars to extreme shooting • Computer Fundas - It’s all about computer basics All the winners will be awarded with certificates and attractive prizes during the closing ceremony. For your further queries, contact:- Mr. Satinder Saini (9988881992) OR email your queries to :- invictus.techfest@gmail.com Authorized By: CoD-S Department LSECA

title: Call for entries: SMART PROGRAMMER “Let’s program the computer to solve things for us!” (LIE-CSE/IT and LSE-CSE/IT) (3/16/2011)
body: “Those who say it can’t be done should stay out of the way of those who are doing it.” A program decides what the computer will do and how. The expertise and skills of the best and the smart can let one exercise full control over the machine via good programs and can make it solve a problem efficiently. If you are such a Smart Programmer, then jump into this fight. The event is open for the students of LIE, LSE and LIECA to contest. title: FIGHT-ENG-FEARS….“Feel the Fear and Do it Anyway” (an inter-school ENG play competition) (3/16/2011)
body: Feel the Fear and Do it Anyway” – The best method to fight any fear is to take positive action against whatever it is that you are afraid of. Is fear of failure stopping you from learning that new skill? If yes, then go ahead and learn it! This is what courage is all about: to act despite the fear. With this belief, Department of Computer Applications, LSECA, had given its students an opportunity to overcome their hesitation and fear of communicating in ENGLISH by organizing an inter-section ENGLISH play competition under the concept of “FIGHT-ENG-FEARS”. After getting the encouragement & appreciation from Honorable Pro-chancellor and observing the tremendous response from students, we are going to organize the same event again but at University level in the form of Inter-school competition ,tentatively on 7th & 8th April, 2011. The general guidelines for the event are as following: 1. Script of the play should be in ENGLISH only. 2. Students themselves will decide the theme and script. 3. Every PLAY should be carrying a message to the society. 4. Team size should not be more than 12 members. 5. Time duration of a play is 15-20 minutes. 6. All performances will be evaluated by a panel of judges. 7. There will be only one team from one school. In case of more than one team, concerned cultural coordinator will finalize one team. 8. The best three teams will be given certificates and prizes. Important: 1. Interested students can give their names to their respective Cultural coordinator by 19th Mar’11. 2. All cultural coordinators are to finalize and submit the theme & participants of play by 21st Mar’11. (All HOS/HODs are requested to encourage their students for participating in this event) For any queries, you can contact faculty event coordinators: Ms Jasveen Kalra (jasveen.kalra@lpu.co.in Mob: 8146300747) OR Ms Mandeep Kaur (mandeep.13695@lpu.co.in Mob: 9988533109) OR Mr Rajeev Kanday (Rajeev.13544@lpu.co.in Mob: 9888235282) Authorized By: HOS Department LSECA

title: Workshop on Bread Making by LSH (3/10/2011)
body: Would you like to become a baker at home? So, here comes the opportunity of a lifetime to learn in a very professional way and that too in your own vicinity. Learn the art of bread making with Chef Karan Berry in this small, hands-on session of just 15 students at block 16(406) on 17/3/11 from 3-5 p.m. Chef Karan has worked with Five-star deluxe Hotel Leela Palace, Bangalore as a Kitchen Executive & now teaching Bakery &Patisserie to the students of hotel management at L.S.H. Over two hours you will be provided with basic understanding of different popular breads and their recipes which you can try at your home. Focassia (Rich Italian bread with olives & sun dried tomatoes) Dinner rolls (small breads having varied shapes and sizes, usually served with soup) Masala bread (spiced bread with varied flavours and seasoning) French baguette (A long French bread with a hard exterior and a soft interior served with curry) Fruit & nut bread (Soft and sweet bread with raisin and walnuts) Confirm your participation by filling & submitting the attached form before 15/3/11. Attachment: Registration form_March 10.doc If you have any questions or queries please don’t hesitate to call Chef Karan Berry at 9501138930. E-mail id- karan.14608@lpu.co.in Authorized By: Office of Deputy Dean Deptt: Hotel Magnagement Lovely School of Hospitality

title: Instruction for Students for Mid Term Examination (Theory) March, 2011. (3/1/2011)
body: 1. IDENTITY CARD IS A MUST: - All candidates must have valid identity cards. Entry to the Examination Room/Hall without Identity Card is strictly prohibited. 2. NO MOBILE PHONES: Any electronic device such as Mobile Phones, Pagers etc are strictly Prohibited in the Examination Room / Hall. Any candidate, in possession of such devices (even in switched off mode), will be placed under UMC and punished as per rules. 3. NO WRITTEN / PRINTED MATERIAL: The candidates must not be in possession of any written / printed material, other wise they will be placed under UMC and punished as per rules. 4. Any thing written on question paper, except Registration No. on any part of the body (e.g. on hand) or clothes / dress of the candidates is strictly prohibited, any violation of this will invite UMC and punishment as per rules. 5. ACCEPT QUESTION PAPER HAVING CORRECT COURSE CODE: It is the responsibility of the candidate to ensure that he accepts the Question Paper of correct Course Code. QUESTION PAPER DISCREPANCY: Any discrepancy in the Question Paper should be reported to Invigilator and SOC immediately or should be reported in written to Examination Division on the same day of Examination. No Question Paper discrepancy will be entertained later. 7. If any candidate is found creating indiscipline or doing misconduct may face the disciplinary action against him or it may lead to the filing of UMC against him. 8. Entry to Examination Hall will be allowed upto 15 minutes after the start of the Exam in case of MTE. title: IEEE students chapter initiated in LPU (2/26/2011)
body: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), the biggest name in any form of engineering related research in the world, has set up a students' chapter in LPU. The chapter was inaugurated by an esteemed guest, Prof. (Dr.) Nalin Sharda, Victoria University, Australia on 30th January 2011. In its first event, IEEE LPU hosted the 11th Quarterly meet of Delhi Section which saw representations from 11 esteemed colleges from North India. IEEE is a name synonymous with up-gradations in technology and the IEEE students chapter vows to live by the same theme. In the weeks to come IEEE will host a band of events to update our fellow students about the latest technological innovations in many fields of engineering. Being a student chapter, the whole thing is managed, organized and hosted directly by the students with a few faculty mentors. The Executive Committee for the same is: Prof. Bhupinder Verma, Branch Counselor Er. Abhishek Gagneja, Branch Mentor Gautam Anand, Chairperson Karan Deep Singh Vice-Chairperson (Externals) Shubham Goyal Vice-Chairperson (internal) Payal Thakur General Secretary Vivek Bhagat Treasurer For any queries regarding IEEE and how to become a member of our team, please feel free to contact the following: gautamanand@ieee.org karandeepsingh13@ieee.org shubhamgoyal@ieee.org Authorized By: Office of HOD Deptt: ECE

title: Seminar on GRE (Change in the test), GMAT & SAT (2/24/2011)
body: A seminar will be organized on 25th February, 2011 in Block 29, Room No. 304 in collaboration with Manya Eduction (P) Ltd. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is a standardized test that is an admission requirement for many graduate programs in the United States and in other English-speaking countries and for English-taught graduate and business programs world-wide. The Graduate Management Admission Test (GMAT) is a computer-adaptive standardized test in mathematics and the English language for measuring aptitude to succeed academically in graduate business studies. Business schools commonly use the test as one of many selection criteria for admission into graduate business administration programs (e.g. MBA, Master of accountancy, etc.) principally in the United States, but also in other English-speaking countries. The SAT Reasoning Test (formerly Scholastic Aptitude Test and Scholastic Assessment Test) is a standardized test for college admissions in the United States. There will be three sessions as follows : 1st : 1:00 – 2:00 pm 2nd : 3:00 – 4:00 pm 3rd: 4:00 – 5:00 pm All students are invited to attend a session as per their availability. Authorized By: Office of HOD Deptt: Extension Education

title: Mid-term (Ist) evaluation of project training of 4th year Biotech Students (Section C77T1) of LST school on March 10, 2011 (2/21/2011)
body: The mid-term evaluation of project training (C77T1) is scheduled on 10th March 2011from 9:30 AM onwards. Kindly note down the following points for evaluations. a) You need to give your presentation as well as a project report in hard copy to be submitted to the panel. b) Project report should contain following things in the same order as mentioned. 1) Cover Page, 2) Declaration Page duly signed by you, 3) Acknowledgement Page duly signed by you, 4) Abstract (applicable in final report after completion of project), 5) Contents, 6) List of Figures, 7) List of Tables, 8) Abbreviations, 9) Motivation, 10) Problem Definition, 10) Introduction, 11) Literature Review, 12) Materials and Methods, 13) Results and Discussion, 14) Conclusion (if any), 15) References In your project report you need to cite references at appropriate places wherever required. Use IEEE format for citing references. Kindly read the attached file “ieeecitationref.pdf” for help The evaluation criteria will be following Amount of work done – 5 marks Quality of work done – 10 marks Quality of written report/presentation – 20 marks Responses to the questions asked – 15 marks Find enclose the formats for making your project reports. Also find enclose the list of students along with their internal mentors. You need to mail to your mentor giving your project details in brief along with the progress you have made in your project till now. Attachment: project_report_formats(3)_21Feb.zip Authorized By: Office of HOD Deptt: Biotechnology LST

title: Call for entries: SMART WRITER "Come, Write for Technology - The Smart way!" (LIE-CSE/IT) (2/21/2011)
body: "You do not know anything clearly, unless you can state it in writing!" It is believed that a pen is mightier than a sword. If you have this might, come use your pen to write something meaningful for technology that has changed computing and, in a way, our life. The department of CSE/IT (LIE) invites entries from the students of LIE-CSE/IT (all sections) for participation in the SMART WRITER, a technical writing competition. Each participant/candidate will have to write a technical article on any one of the topics (given on-the-spot) related to current trends and technology. The sheets for writing will be provided by us. The maximum time allowed for writing will be 1 hour. Interested students must give their names to respective class in-charges positively by 26 -Feb-2011. All concerned class in-charges are required to submit the list of entries positively to Mr. Sumit Mittu, Lecturer, LIE - CSE/IT through email (sumit.12735@lpu.co.in) by 10 AM of 28-Feb-2011. title: Seminar on GRE (Change in the test), GMAT & SAT (2/17/2011)
body: A seminar will be organized on 25th February, 2011 in Block 29, Room No. 304 in collaboration with Manya Eduction (P) Ltd. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is a standardized test that is an admission requirement for many graduate programs in the United States and in other English-speaking countries and for English-taught graduate and business programs world-wide. The Graduate Management Admission Test (GMAT) is a computer-adaptive standardized test in mathematics and the English language for measuring aptitude to succeed academically in graduate business studies. Business schools commonly use the test as one of many selection criteria for admission into graduate business administration programs (e.g. MBA, Master of accountancy, etc.) principally in the United States, but also in other English-speaking countries. The SAT Reasoning Test (formerly Scholastic Aptitude Test and Scholastic Assessment Test) is a standardized test for college admissions in the United States. There will be three sessions as follows : 1st : 1:00 – 2:00 pm 2nd : 3:00 – 4:00 pm 3rd: 4:00 – 5:00 pm All students are invited to attend a session as per their availability. Authorized By: Office of HOD Deptt : Extension Education

title: ATTENTION: Students selected in AON Hewitt (2/16/2011)
body: This is with reference to the selection done by M/s AON Hewitt in the placement process conducted on 8th& 9th January. This is to inform you that the 1st batch of 47 selected B Tech & MCA students has already joined on 10th Feb as intern for Industrial Training starting from February. These students were available for immediate joining. At the time of interaction on 4th Feb, there was a concern raised about the joining/offer letter of the students selected for June/July batch. AON Hewitt will release the offer letters to the Selected/Shortlisted students (list is attached for reference) based on their business requirement. As on today they cannot forecast the date of joining for these students as they have not got the confirmation from the business about the future requirement. As the requirement comes up, they will release the offer letters to these selected/shortlisted students. I would like to inform you that there is no further round of interview pending for these students, only the offer letters are pending. As some concerns were voiced about the offer letters and joining, the University has decided that all students selected/shortlisted can sit for the upcoming Placement Drives subject to following conditions: • In case any student who has not been offered any job other than AON HEWITT and is selected in any subsequent drive, then it will be considered as 1st offer. • The moment the student gets the offer letter from AON Hewitt, then this will be considered as 2nd offer and the choice will be given to the student to opt for any one between the two offers within 2 days of receipt of 2nd offer. In case, no information is received from the student within 2 days of communication/receipt of 2nd offer; then the first offer will automatically stand cancelled and surrendered. • If any student gets a second offer before he gets the AON Hewitt offer letter then his AON Hewitt offer and the first offer will get surrendered automatically. Thus his first offer and AON HEWITT will stand cancelled and it would be his second offer that he would have to join. If you have any confusion or need clarity or want to discuss your query in detail then you can attend the doubt clearing session on 21st Feb at Block 29 – 402, Time – 4:00 PM We at placement cell always intend to get the best placement for our students. Attachment: AON Hewitt_Final Result_16Feb.xls Authorized By: Office of Director Deptt: DSCS

title: Results for Syntel Recruitment Drive. (2/11/2011)
body: Congratulations to all the students appearing in the attached list…… Selected students are eligible to join Syntel, subject to theirs fulfilling the eligibility criteria mentioned below: a) The candidate should not have any examination backlogs; b) The candidate should have obtained minimum of 50% marks in 10th and 12th standards and Graduation. c) The candidate should be Indian citizens and should be eligible to hold valid Indian passports; d) The candidate should be medically (physically and mentally) fit. The Company reserves the right to ask the candidate to undergo medical examination as and when considered necessary; e) The candidate should not have been punished by any authority (including the college) or convicted by any court for any ragging incident and neither should the candidate be facing any action from law enforcement agencies in relation to any crime (e.g., police enquiry, pending court case etc); f) The candidate should not have been convicted by any court for any crime; and g) The background verification of all records/ references of the candidate conducted by the Company should be clear, satisfactory, free from ambiguity and in accordance with the policies of the Company prevalent from time to time. The decision of the Company shall be final and binding in this regard. Attachment: Syntel_final_Result(11Feb).xls Authorized By: Office of Director Deptt: Division of Student Career Services

title: Applications for Italian Scholarships (2/9/2011)
body: Italian Trade Commission has offered a rare scholarship opportunity for our students. It includes all expenses paid 2 weeks trip to Italy. To participate in this scholarship Department is inviting application from the interested students of 3rd year Mechanical Engineering Department for writing a research/technical paper on the following topics 1 The use of Computer Aided Design (CAD), to model and analyze machine components so as to design against fatigue. 2 Mechanical Engineering and its impact on: sustainable engineering technologies, nanotechnology, bio medical technology, aeronautics & aerospace, motor vehicles and biomimetics. 3 Robotics engineering in the mining, defense, manufacturing and Aerospace industries. 4 Thermodynamics and the design of nuclear and solar power plants, refrigerators, Air Conditioners and Propulsion Systems. 5 Mechanical Engineering and their work in manufacturing plants 6 Oversight of the daily operations of a manufacturing plant with an emphasis on finding the most efficient way to convert raw materials into consumer goods. You are advised to write a write up of about 500 words, about the any topic given above. You can consult the undersigned for any clarification. The applications should be submitted by 09- 02 -11.Shortlisted Students will further need to go to Delhi for interview at Italian High Commission. Faculty Resource person: Mr. Gurpreet Singh Phull 14-204 LSE ME Authorized By: Dr. L. R. Gupta HoF LFTS 01824506222-507333

title: FIGHT-ENG-FEARS….“Feel the Fear and Do it Anyway” (2/7/2011)
body: Feel the Fear and Do it Anyway” – The best method to fight any fear is to take positive action against whatever it is that you are afraid of. Is fear of failure stopping you from learning that new skill? Go ahead and learn it! This is what courage is all about: to act despite the fear. With this belief, Department of Computer Applications, LSECA, is giving its students, an opportunity to overcome their hesitation and fear of communicating in ENGLISH by starting a series of events under this new initiative named as “FIGHT-ENG-FEARS”. Aim of this initiative is to encourage students to overcome their hesitation and fear of communicating in ENGLISH language. The first activity, in this series, is an inter-section English Play/Skit competition to be held as per following schedule: Date: 11th Feb ’2011 Time: 2:00 PM Venue: Main Auditorium Important: All Class in-charges and class Representatives are to coordinate for their respective section and must finalize and submit script and list of participating students by 8th Feb 2011 to the faculty event coordinators. title: Applications for Italian Scholarships (2/4/2011)
body: Italian Trade Commission has offered a rare scholarship opportunity for our students. It includes all expenses paid 2 weeks trip to Italy. To participate in this scholarship Department is inviting application from the interested students of 3rd year Mechanical Engineering Department for writing a research/technical paper on the following topics 1 The use of Computer Aided Design (CAD), to model and analyze machine components so as to design against fatigue. 2 Mechanical Engineering and its impact on: sustainable engineering technologies, nanotechnology, bio medical technology, aeronautics & aerospace, motor vehicles and biomimetics. 3 Robotics engineering in the mining, defense, manufacturing and Aerospace industries. 4 Thermodynamics and the design of nuclear and solar power plants, refrigerators, Air Conditioners and Propulsion Systems. 5 Mechanical Engineering and their work in manufacturing plants 6 Oversight of the daily operations of a manufacturing plant with an emphasis on finding the most efficient way to convert raw materials into consumer goods. You are advised to write a write up of about 500 words, about the any topic given above. You can consult the undersigned for any clarification. The applications should be submitted by 09- 02 -11.Shortlisted Students will further need to go to Delhi for interview at Italian High Commission. Faculty Resource person: Mr. Gurpreet Singh Phull 14-204 LSE ME Authorized By: Dr. L. R. Gupta HoF LFTS 1105 01824506222-507333

title: Applications for Italian Scholarships (1/27/2011)
body: Italian Trade Commission has offered a rare scholarship opportunity for our students. It includes all expenses paid 2 weeks trip to Italy. To participate in this scholarship Department is inviting application from the interested students of 3rd year Mechanical Engineering Department for writing a research/technical paper on the following topics 1 The use of Computer Aided Design (CAD), to model and analyze machine components so as to design against fatigue. 2 Mechanical Engineering and its impact on: sustainable engineering technologies, nanotechnology, bio medical technology, aeronautics & aerospace, motor vehicles and biomimetics. 3 Robotics engineering in the mining, defense, manufacturing and Aerospace industries. 4 Thermodynamics and the design of nuclear and solar power plants, refrigerators, Air Conditioners and Propulsion Systems. 5 Mechanical Engineering and their work in manufacturing plants 6 Oversight of the daily operations of a manufacturing plant with an emphasis on finding the most efficient way to convert raw materials into consumer goods. You are advised to write a write up of about 500 words, about the any topic given above. You can consult the undersigned for any clarification. The applications should be submitted by 29- 01 -11.Shortlisted Students will further need to go to Delhi for interview at Italian High Commission. Faculty Resource person: Mr. Gurpreet Singh Phull 14-204 LSE ME Authorized By: Dr. L. R. Gupta HoF LFTS 1105 01824506222-507333

title: FIGHT-ENG-FEARS….“Feel the Fear and Do it Anyway” (1/25/2011)
body: Feel the Fear and Do it Anyway” – The best method to fight any fear is to take positive action against whatever it is that you are afraid of. Is fear of failure stopping you from learning that new skill? Go ahead and learn it! This is what courage is all about: to act despite the fear. With this belief, Department of Computer Applications, LSECA, is giving its students, an opportunity to overcome their hesitation and fear of communicating in ENGLISH by starting a series of events under this new initiative named as “FIGHT-ENG-FEARS”. Aim of this initiative is to encourage students to overcome their hesitation and fear of communicating in ENGLISH language. The first activity, in this series, is an inter-section English Play/Skit competition as per following: 1. Script of the play should be in ENGLISH only. 2. Students themselves will decide the theme and script. 3. Every SKIT/PLAY should be carrying a message to the society. 4. Team size may consist of 8-10 members. 5. Time duration of a play is 15-20 minutes. 6. All performances will be evaluated by a panel of judges. 7. There will be one team each from the sections (D37D1,D37D2,D3801,D3802 and D3912) Attachment: FFEARS.jpg Important: All Class in-charges and class Representatives are to coordinate for their respective section and must finalize and submit theme, script and list of participating students by 28th Jan’2011 to the faculty event coordinators in 34-209. Faculty Event Coordinators: Ms Mandeep Kaur & Ms Jasveen Kalra Authorized By: Pawan Kumar, CoD-S, Deptt of Computer Applications, LSECA

body: In order to improve the skills of programming with C++ and boost the employability of students, the department of CSE/IT is about launch an exercise workbook on the course CSE202: OBJECT ORIENTED PROGRAMMING. For an analysis of the difficulty level of the workbook, a review activity is going to be performed. From amongst the sections B6912, C1911, C1912, C6913, C6914, F1902, G1901, H1001 and M6902, 25 students are nominated to participate in this process of analysis. These students are supposed to prepare for (revise) the concepts of C++ programming. Then they will take an objective-type test comprising of problems (extracted out of the workbook) of the type MCQs, Debugging/Output prediction, Yes/No and Fill in the blanks, etc. The test activity would be conducted on Saturday, January 29, 2011 in room 14-404 from 3PM – 5PM. The list of students from these sections who are nominated to participate in this exercise and take the objective-type test is attached alongwith this announcement. title: “Trainer Hunt: Peer-to-Peer Training” (1/15/2011)
body: Department of Computer Applications, after successfully implementing the concept of Peer-to-Peer training in the previous term for 2011 batch, is going to start the same for 2012 passing out batch. The objective is to form student groups who can conduct training/grooming sessions for fellow students on areas that are deemed important from placement or employability perspective. • These sessions will be conducted by the students under the guidance of faculty. • As a trainer, Students will get an opportunity to show-case their talent and learn more. • Training areas are C, C++, Java, Data Structures, DBMS, Computer Networks, Quantitative Aptitude, Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning or any other, deemed beneficial for students. Eligibility: All regular students of LPU are eligible to apply. Selection Process: Panel Interview and/or demo lecture. Excellent performers would be considered for a letter of appreciation. All students, interested and confident of doing as a trainer, can give their names by 21st Jan, 2011 to: Mr. Rajeev Kanday, Placement Coordinator at Rajeev.13544@lpu.co.in(Mobile:9888235282, 9501110420) Mr. Avinish Kumar, Placement Co-Coordinator at avinish.14600@lpu.co.in (Mobile: 07837257304) Authorized By: Pawan Kumar, CoD-S, Computer Applications, LSECA

title: Placement Policy – Reopening of Registration for the students passing out in 2011 (1/11/2011)
body: Refer subject above PLEASE NOTE THAT THIS NOTICE IS MEANT ONLY FOR STUDENTS PASSING OUT IN 2011 The option of registering for the placement assistance, as per provisions of Placement Policy, was made available to the students from June 2010 onwards and remained available at various intervals up to middle of September 2010 and then again in December 2010. Despite the option remaining alive for months, a good number of students did not register for the same. It was made clear in the policy that university will offer placement assistance to only those students who opt for the same. As such all students who have not opted for placement policy are, therefore, not eligible for taking part in any placement process. However, as a special gesture, the university is allowing all such students to register for placement policy and to take part in the placement drives subject to following conditions: 1. Producing a signed undertaking from their parents that their ward will adhere to all prescribed conditions including stipulated attendance in all placement related activities. 2. Complete filling up of registration form on the UMS by 12th January till 1200 hours. 3. The last date for receipt of signed undertaking from parents is 18th January 2011. 4. The appointment offers, if any, received in the meantime shall be provisional. The Proforma for undertaking is attached herewith. Attachment: UNDERTAKING_FORMAT_1.doc The placement policy registration is available on students’ UMS from 10th January to 12th January till 1200 hours. After the students have registered and filled the registration form in all respects, the drives would be visible to them and they can mark their preference for individual drives as per their eligibility. Students are required to get the undertaking verified from their Teacher Placement Coordinator/HOD. QUERIES REGARDING FRESH REGISTRATION/AMENDMENT ETC IN THE REGISTRATION FORM EITHER IN PERSON OR IN WRITING WILL NOT BE ENTERTAINED AFTER 12TH JANUARY Authorized By: Mr. Navein Juneja Director Division of Student Career Services 13079 01824 -501230

Student can go through his/her Evaluated Answer Script and write request / remark on the space provided on the Front Page of the Answer Sheet with Pencil only. 3. Student is allowed to write only three type of remarks as mentioned below: (a) Any question or part thereof not graded. (b) Marks awarded for a question does not match with the marks written on the front page. (c) Any type of totaling or clerical mistake 6. Re-grading / Rectification of error (Sr. No. 5a) will be done by the concerned evaluator who has originally graded the particular question and a comment shall be made on the answer sheet under the signature of the evaluator 7. The scope for re-grading will be restricted strictly to the comments of the students on the cover of the answer-book during the process of showing answer sheets to the students. If any student does not abide by the clauses mentioned above, UMC may be filed against him. Writing with a pen or writing anywhere other than at specified place or not returning the Answer Sheets or any other disobedience will result in UMC case. For any further clarification you may contact Examination Division (Room No.29-306) Authorized By: Navdeep Dhaliwal Deputy Dean Examination Division 11061 01824-500886

title: Part-Time Joint Certification Program with National Stock Exchange (NSE) (1/2/2011)
body: LPU is pleased to announce a part time joint certification program with National Stock Exchange - NSE Certified Capital Market Professional (NCCMP). The program is open for all students and faculty members. The students will be entitled to fee discount of Rs.2500/- and faculty members will be entitled to a fee discount of Rs.5000/- on the NSE prescribed registration fee of Rs.15000/- . Program Highlights: • Part time program with NSE curriculum, study material and examinations • Lectures by Industry Experts and NSE Experts. • 80 hours of teaching covering Financial Markets, Derivatives, Trading System, Fundamental Analysis, Technical Analysis, Market Operations and Currency Futures. • 20 hours of practical training with broker for hands on experience in trading and other operations. • Improves employment prospects in financial services companies. • Enhances business opportunities for self employed professionals. • Prepares participants for NCFM certifications. title: NOTICE (1/1/2011)
body: • The students can now view their marks of End Term Examinations (December, 2010) on UMS. • Scrutiny is scheduled on 4th January, 2011. The students are required to follow the below mentioned instructions for Scrutiny: - 1. Students are required to sit according to the Roll No. in the assigned room already displayed in the UMS for scrutiny on dated 04-01-2011. 2. Students have to use only LEAD PENCILONLY during the scrutiny, if any student found with any sort of pen during the scrutiny it will be a case of UMC. 3. Students are required to check their answer sheets of all the courses in a stipulated time of 30 MINUTES ONLY during the scrutiny. 4. During Scrutiny students can write (a) Totaling is wrong. (b) A particular Question is unchecked. (c) Part of a particular Question is unchecked. kind of comments in the column provided in the answer sheets: 5. After scrutiny students have to return back all the answer sheets to the invigilator after writing comments in the space provided in the answer sheet if any rectification is there in any course. 6. If a student is not satisfied with the evaluation of a particular course then they have to apply for re-evaluation which is a different process. Regarding re-evaluation students have to consult the Examination Department. 7. For students who have been also appeared for backlog courses, scrutiny is scheduled in room no 28-101 between 11:00-2:00. 8. Students are not allowed to keep their bags, mobiles and other belongings with them during Scrutiny. For any further clarification you may contact Dr. Ramesh Thakur, COD-F (Chemistry) Division of Examination Authorized By: Dr. Lovi Raj Gupta Sr. Dean (LFTS)
